evidence.summary: Header comment describes the app as reading lists and 1-5 star ratings.
SQLite via sqlite3 with a hard-coded file readr.db; books table: id integer primary key, title text not null (no author).
lists table (id integer primary key, name text not null) and list_books join table (list_id references lists(id), book_id references books(id)) with no primary key or uniqueness.
ratings table: book_id integer references books(id), stars integer; no CHECK constraint, no primary key, no uniqueness.
rate(book_id, stars) raises ValueError unless stars is one of 1-5, then appends a ratings row.
add_to_list(list_id, book_id) inserts a list_books row with no check for duplicates or that the list and book exist.
No function creates, renames or deletes lists or books, reads anything back, or removes a book from a list; no HTTP, CLI or UI entry point; no commit; no users or auth.

architecture.backend: a single Python module of data functions, no entry point

features.name: Reading lists
features.description: Put books on named reading lists.
features.observed_behaviour: add_to_list(list_id, book_id) appends a list_books row. Lists have a name. Nothing in the code creates a list, shows a list or removes a book from one.
features.business_logic: list name required; a book may be added to the same list twice; no existence checks.
features.integration: Needs Book from the shared library; needs list ownership in a multi-user app.

features.name: Rate a book (1-5 stars)
features.description: Give a book a star rating from 1 to 5.
features.observed_behaviour: rate(book_id, stars) rejects anything outside 1-5 with ValueError, then appends a ratings row.
features.business_logic: stars 1..5 checked in code only (no database constraint); every call appends.

error_handling.behaviour: ValueError('1 to 5 stars') raised to the caller

error_handling.case: adding to a missing list or book, or twice

error_handling.behaviour: no commit is ever made, so writes are lost when the connection closes (inferred from sqlite3 behaviour; not run)

unknowns: How lists and books are created or read: the code has no function for it and no entry point. Only the user can say what called these functions.
Whether a readr.db with real data exists (needed only if data will be imported).
Runtime behaviour was not observed: running source code was not approved.
